title: Use of human arguments against unbelievers and atheists; philosophical preparation then providence
pass_a_gloss: XIII. The use of arguments of this sort is properly for convincing unbelievers and atheists. 1. The unbeliever either denies that God is, is one, truthful, just and good, that the soul is immortal, and that there will be another right after this life: or he concedes. 2. If he has denied, the theologian will be able to do nothing against him by theological habit. 3. Wherefore he is to be convinced by philosophical habit from principles drawn out from the nature of things. 4. If he has conceded, FIRST the vanity of his religion is to be shown. 5. SECOND it is to be proposed that God for his infinite goodness bears the greatest care of man. 6. The matter is plain from politics: it would be absurd that those things which pertain to earthly life be abundantly furnished by providence, but those which make for eternal life be neglected. 7. THIRD after it has been proved that God cares for the salvation of men, some doctrine divinely revealed must be given.
pass_b_english: XIII. The use of such arguments is properly to convince unbelievers and atheists. Against true Christians who watch for their souls there is no need of them.

1. The unbeliever either denies that God is, that He is one, truthful, just and good, that the soul is immortal, and that there will be another life — or he grants these. 2. If he denies them, the theologian can do nothing in the theological habit. 3. Therefore convince him in the philosophical habit from nature's principles. 4. If he grants them, first show his religion's vanity. 5. Second, propose that God of infinite goodness takes greatest care of the human being — and that it would clash with that goodness never to reveal His will concerning salvation. 6. Politics makes it plain: providence is credited with kingdoms' preservation; it would be absurd to supply earthly life richly while neglecting eternal life for an immortal soul. 7. Third, once God's care for salvation is proved, some divinely revealed doctrine showing the way to eternal life must be given.
source_text: XIII. Usus argumentorum horum talium est proprie ad convincendum infideles & atheos. 1. Infidelis aut negat Deum… aut concedit. 2–3. Si negat, habitu philosophico… 4–7. Si concedit: vanitas suae religionis; Dei cura salutis; providentia terrena absque aeterna absurda; ergo doctrina divinitus revelata dari debet.
